Ankh Acetylation Prediction — Interpretation Report

Source: {notebook_name}  |  Embeddings: Ankh protein language model (768-dim)  |  Task: binary protein-level acetylation classification

1. Dataset

Proteins from the manually curated UniProt/Swiss-Prot proteome were split into two mutually exclusive classes using the free-text Post-translational modification column:

  • Positive (acetylated): entry contains the string acetyl in the PTM field
  • Negative (not acetylated): no acetylation mention in the PTM field

Figure 1. Class distribution. Acetylated proteins represent 1.9% of the dataset.

Class imbalance note: With 1.9% positive examples, PR-AUC (Average Precision) is a key secondary metric. A random classifier achieves PR-AUC ≈ 0.019. Models are trained with imbalance corrections (class_weight="balanced" for LR; BCEWithLogitsLoss pos_weight for MLP).

2. Methods

2.1 Embeddings

Precomputed Ankh protein language model embeddings (768-dim) were loaded from a pre-built NPZ cache. Two global sequence representations:

  • Max pooling — element-wise maximum across residues
  • Attention pooling — learned weighted average across residues

Features were z-score normalised (StandardScaler) using training statistics only.

5. Interpretation

5.1 Overall Performance

Best model (Mlp + ATTN) achieves ROC-AUC=0.8132, PR-AUC=0.2214, F1=0.2222, MCC=0.2263. PR-AUC of 0.2214 vs random baseline 0.019 represents 11.5× improvement over chance.

5.2 Pooling Comparison

Attention vs max-pool delta: MLP ++0.038, LR ++0.050 (PR-AUC).

5.3 Acetylation as a Prediction Target

  • Label source: Free-text PTM field — may include N-terminal acetylation, lysine acetylation, and other acetyl modifications in one label.
  • Imbalance: Only 1.9% of proteins carry an acetylation annotation. This makes PR-AUC critical; ROC-AUC can be misleadingly high.
  • Bottleneck: Global pooling discards residue-position information; acetylation signals (e.g., N-terminal Ala/Met motifs) are inherently local.

6. Recommendations

  1. Stratify by acetylation type (N-terminal vs lysine).
  2. Train residue-level classifiers on per-token embeddings for site prediction.
  3. Replace single 80/20 split with 5-fold cross-validation.
  4. Benchmark against other PLMs (Ankh / ESM2 / ProtT5).
